title: 1 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 13.

questions.question: Who came out of Judah by the word of the LORD unto Bethel?
options: A man of God
King Jeroboam
An old prophet
An angel
questions.correctAnswer: A man of God
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:1 states that a man of God came out of Judah by the word of the LORD unto Bethel.

questions.question: What was Jeroboam doing by the altar in Bethel?
options: Burning incense
Offering a sacrifice
Praying
Reading the law
questions.correctAnswer: Burning incense
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 13:1, Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense.

questions.question: What did the man of God say would happen to the altar?
options: It shall be rent and ashes poured out
It shall be destroyed by fire
It shall be moved to Jerusalem
It shall be covered with gold
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be rent and ashes poured out
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:3 records the sign given by the man of God that the altar shall be rent and the ashes poured out.

questions.question: What happened to King Jeroboam's hand when he tried to seize the man of God?
options: His hand dried up and he could not pull it back
His hand was burned
His hand was healed immediately
His hand was covered with scales
questions.correctAnswer: His hand dried up and he could not pull it back
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:4 states that Jeroboam's hand dried up so that he could not pull it back when he put it forth to seize the man of God.

questions.question: True or False: The altar was not affected after the man of God's prophecy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:5 confirms that the altar was rent and the ashes poured out as the man of God said.

questions.question: What did King Jeroboam ask the man of God to do after his hand was restored?
options: Pray for him to restore his hand
Leave Bethel immediately
Burn incense with him
Build a new altar
questions.correctAnswer: Pray for him to restore his hand
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:6 shows that Jeroboam asked the man of God to pray for the restoration of his hand, which was done.

questions.question: What did Jeroboam offer the man of God if he would come home with him?
options: A reward
Half his kingdom
A new altar
A priestly position
questions.correctAnswer: A reward
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:7 records that Jeroboam said he would give the man of God a reward if he came home with him.

questions.question: True or False: The man of God agreed to eat bread and drink water in Bethel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:8-9 states the man of God refused to eat bread or drink water in that place as commanded by the word of the LORD.

questions.question: How did the man of God return after speaking at Bethel?
options: By another way, not the same path he came
By the same way he came
He stayed in Bethel
He was taken by the old prophet
questions.correctAnswer: By another way, not the same path he came
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:10 explains that the man of God returned another way, not by the way he came to Bethel.

questions.question: Who lived in Bethel and heard about the man of God's works?
options: An old prophet
Jeroboam
The priests
The king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: An old prophet
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:11 tells us that an old prophet lived in Bethel and his sons reported the works of the man of God to him.

questions.question: What did the old prophet ask his sons regarding the man of God?
options: What way did he go?
If he ate bread
If he was a liar
If Jeroboam was angry
questions.correctAnswer: What way did he go?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:12 shows the old prophet asking his sons what way the man of God went.

questions.question: True or False: The man of God was commanded by the LORD to eat bread and drink water in Bethel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:9 clearly states the man of God was charged not to eat bread or drink water in that place.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 13, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Do not eat bread or drink water in Bethel
Cry against the altar in the word of the LORD
Bring the man of God back to eat bread
Restore Jeroboam’s hand by prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Cry against the altar in the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:2 shows the man of God crying against the altar first; the other instructions or events come afterward.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of the old prophet were witnesses to the man of God's path after Bethel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:12 states the sons had seen the way the man of God went, confirming they were witnesses.

questions.question: What did the man of God refuse to do even if offered half the king's house?
options: Go in with the king and eat or drink in Bethel
Pray for the king’s hand
Return by the same way he came
Cry against the altar
questions.correctAnswer: Go in with the king and eat or drink in Bethel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:8 records the man of God's refusal to enter with the king or eat and drink there, even if offered half the house.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the old prophet say when his sons told him about the man of God from Judah and his actions in Bethel?
options: He asked what way the man of God went
He told them to ignore the man of God
He ordered his sons to capture the man of God
He said the man of God was a false prophet
questions.correctAnswer: He asked what way the man of God went
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:12 records that the old prophet asked his sons, 'What way went he?' after they told him about the man of God's actions and words.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 13, why did the man of God refuse to eat bread or drink water in Bethel?
options: Because the king commanded him not to
Because the LORD had charged him not to do so
Because he was fasting for three days
Because the old prophet forbade it
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had charged him not to do so
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 13:9 and 13:17, the man of God explains that the LORD commanded him neither to eat bread nor drink water in that place.

questions.question: How does the interaction between the old prophet and the man of God teach about obedience and trust in God's word?
options: It shows that we must obey every prophet we meet without question
It teaches that one should only trust in the original command from God and not be misled by others
It encourages following any angel's message regardless of previous instructions
It suggests that eating and drinking are always permissible when invited
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that one should only trust in the original command from God and not be misled by others
questions.explanation: The man of God disobeyed the original command from God by trusting the old prophet's lie, showing the importance of adhering to God's direct instructions (1 Kings 13:16-18, 21).

questions.question: What was the consequence for the man of God eating bread and drinking water in Bethel, contrary to God's command?
options: He was forgiven immediately
He was killed by a lion on the way
He was imprisoned by the king
He was sent back to Judah without punishment
questions.correctAnswer: He was killed by a lion on the way
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:24 states that after eating and drinking, the man of God was slain by a lion as a direct consequence of disobedience (1 Kings 13:21-24).

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 13:21-22 teach about the seriousness of disobedience to God's commands?
options: Disobedience leads to immediate joyful reward
Disobedience results in severe consequences like death and dishonor
Disobedience is overlooked if done unknowingly
Disobedience only affects the disobedient person’s family
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience results in severe consequences like death and dishonor
questions.explanation: Verses 21 and 22 show God’s judgment for disobedience: the man’s body would not be buried with his ancestors, and he would face death, emphasizing obedience's importance.

questions.question: What action did the old prophet take after hearing of the man of God's death by the lion?
options: He ignored the news
He went to find the man's body and buried it
He rejoiced over the death
He reported it to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He went to find the man's body and buried it
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:27-30 describes how the old prophet saddled his ass, found the man’s body with the lion and ass standing by, and then took up the body to bury it and mourn.

questions.question: Based on 1 Kings 13:31-32, what did the old prophet request regarding his burial and why?
options: To be buried in his own house for safety
To be buried beside the man of God because the prophecy against the altar would surely come to pass
To be buried in the city to be remembered by many
To be buried in an unknown place
questions.correctAnswer: To be buried beside the man of God because the prophecy against the altar would surely come to pass
questions.explanation: The old prophet asked to be buried in the same tomb as the man of God, believing the prophecy against the altar and high places would come to pass, as stated in verses 31-32.

questions.question: How does the story of the man of God's disobedience teach us about the importance of integrity in following God's commands?
options: It shows that partial obedience is acceptable
It highlights that double-mindedness and trusting lies lead to downfall
It suggests that God is lenient with disobedience
It teaches that human reasoning is superior to God's word
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights that double-mindedness and trusting lies lead to downfall
questions.explanation: The man of God's failure to maintain integrity by obeying God's direct command and instead trusting a false message led to his death (1 Kings 13:18-22), showing the necessity of steadfast obedience.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 13:23-24 demonstrate about consequences following disobedience after the command?
options: Consequences are delayed until after the disobedient person leaves the place
Consequences can be avoided by quick repentance
Consequences are always temporary and symbolic
Consequences do not affect others
questions.correctAnswer: Consequences are delayed until after the disobedient person leaves the place
questions.explanation: After eating and drinking, the man of God saddled his ass and left, and then the lion met and killed him, showing consequences can come after the act of disobedience (1 Kings 13:23-24).

questions.question: True or False: The old prophet's lie about an angel commanding the man of God to return and eat bread was a test from God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:18 explicitly states the old prophet lied to the man of God; the text does not indicate this was a test from God but deception.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam continued in his evil ways and did not repent after the events with the man of God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:33 states Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way but continued to consecrate priests from the lowest people, showing no repentance.

questions.question: True or False: The man of God obeyed the old prophet's invitation because he truly believed the message from the angel was from the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 13:18-19, the man of God was deceived by the old prophet's claim of an angelic message and went back with him, indicating he believed the message was from the LORD.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 13:26 teach us about God's justice and fulfillment of His word?
options: God ignores disobedience if repentance is shown
God delivers the disobedient to judgment as He promised
God rewards those who share falsehoods
God punishes only the innocent
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers the disobedient to judgment as He promised
questions.explanation: The old prophet explains in verse 26 that the man of God was delivered to the lion because he disobeyed the word of the LORD, fulfilling God's judgment.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 13:15-17 teach about the importance of following God's explicit instructions rather than human persuasion?
options: Human persuasion is always more reliable than God's word
God's explicit commands must be obeyed even if humans invite otherwise
God's commands are flexible depending on circumstances
Human invitation is a sign of God's blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God's explicit commands must be obeyed even if humans invite otherwise
questions.explanation: The man of God refused to eat or drink despite the old prophet's invitation because God had commanded otherwise, emphasizing obedience to God's direct commands over human persuasion (1 Kings 13:16-17).

questions.question: What practical lesson about temptation and integrity can Christians learn from the man of God's experience in 1 Kings 13?
options: Temptations should be ignored if they come from strangers
Even a prophet can fall if they do not firmly stand on God's word
It is acceptable to bend God's commands if circumstances require
One should always trust other believers over God's word
questions.correctAnswer: Even a prophet can fall if they do not firmly stand on God's word
questions.explanation: The man of God was led astray by a false prophet’s lie and disobeyed God’s command, showing that steadfastness in God's word is essential to resist temptation and maintain integrity (1 Kings 13:18-22).

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 13.

questions.question: What did the lion do when it met the man of God after he left the old prophet's house?
options: It slew him and stood by his carcass
It ate his carcass and left
It ignored him and walked away
It followed him without attacking
questions.correctAnswer: It slew him and stood by his carcass
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 13:24, the lion met the man of God by the way, slew him, and stood by his carcass.

questions.question: What command did the man of God receive from the LORD about eating and drinking in the place he came to Bethel?
options: Do not eat bread nor drink water there
Eat bread but do not drink water
Drink water but do not eat bread
Eat and drink freely at Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: Do not eat bread nor drink water there
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:9 states the man of God was commanded by the LORD not to eat bread nor drink water in that place.

questions.question: How did the old prophet deceive the man of God?
options: He lied that an angel told him to bring the man of God back to eat and drink
He threatened him with death if he did not return
He offered him a large reward for returning
He told the king to imprison him
questions.correctAnswer: He lied that an angel told him to bring the man of God back to eat and drink
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 13:18, the old prophet said he was also a prophet and that an angel told him to bring the man of God back, which was a lie.

questions.question: What was the consequence for the man of God's disobedience to the LORD's command?
options: His carcass would not be buried in his fathers' sepulchre
He would be king of Judah
He would be healed and rewarded
He would become a priest in Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: His carcass would not be buried in his fathers' sepulchre
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:22 states the LORD declared the man's carcass would not come to the sepulchre of his fathers because he disobeyed.

questions.question: What did the old prophet do after finding the carcass of the man of God?
options: He took up the carcass, laid it on his ass, and brought it back to the city
He left the carcass and fled the city
He burned the carcass and mourned
He reported it to King Jeroboam
questions.correctAnswer: He took up the carcass, laid it on his ass, and brought it back to the city
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 13:29, the old prophet took up the carcass, laid it on the ass, and brought it back to the city.

questions.question: What request did the old prophet make concerning his own burial?
options: To be buried in the sepulchre where the man of God was buried
To be buried in his own field far away
To be cremated and scattered at Bethel
To be buried with King Jeroboam
questions.correctAnswer: To be buried in the sepulchre where the man of God was buried
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:31 shows the old prophet asked his sons to bury him beside the man of God’s bones when he died.

questions.question: What was the ultimate fate of Jeroboam's house as a result of his sins?
options: It would be cut off and destroyed from the face of the earth
It would flourish and gain many kings
It would be blessed by the LORD forever
It would rule over all Israel unchallenged
questions.correctAnswer: It would be cut off and destroyed from the face of the earth
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:34 declares the sin of Jeroboam’s house led to its destruction from the earth.

questions.question: How did Jeroboam respond to the prophecy against his altar in Bethel after these events?
options: He did not repent and continued to consecrate lowly people as priests
He destroyed the altar immediately
He repented and returned to the LORD
He went into exile
questions.correctAnswer: He did not repent and continued to consecrate lowly people as priests
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:33 states Jeroboam returned not from his evil way but consecrated even the lowest of the people as priests.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in the narrative where the man of God disobeys the word of the LORD and is killed by a lion?
options: Foreshadowing
Chiasm
Parallelism
Alliteration
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The death of the man of God by the lion foreshadows the consequences of disobedience to God’s commands, as seen in 1 Kings 13:24 and 13:26.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of disobedience and punishment like the man of God in 1 Kings 13?
options: Numbers 20:12
Genesis 1:1
Psalm 23
John 3:16
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 20:12
questions.explanation: Numbers 20:12 recounts Moses’ disobedience and consequent punishment, echoing the theme of 1 Kings 13:21-24 where disobedience leads to death.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated 'carcase' in this chapter?
options: It emphasizes the lifeless body as a testimony of judgment
It means a living animal
It refers to a temple altar
It signifies a prophetic message
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the lifeless body as a testimony of judgment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'carcase' (נֶפֶשׁ, often translated as 'dead body') highlights the physical consequence of disobedience as in 1 Kings 13:24 and 13:26.

questions.question: How does the narrative of the man of God relate typologically to later New Testament teachings?
options: It serves as a warning about obedience, similar to Christ’s teachings on following God’s commands
It predicts the coming of John the Baptist
It foreshadows the building of the temple by Solomon
It symbolizes the resurrection of Lazarus
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a warning about obedience, similar to Christ’s teachings on following God’s commands
questions.explanation: The man of God's story in 1 Kings 13 emphasizes obedience, a theme Jesus reiterates in passages like John 14:15, connecting Old Testament warnings with New Testament teachings.

questions.question: True or False: The lion ate the carcass of the man of God and then left the ass unharmed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:28 explicitly states the lion had not eaten the carcass nor torn the ass, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: The old prophet who brought the man of God back lied about receiving a message from an angel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 13:18, the old prophet admits he lied about an angel's command, making this statement true.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the theme of judgment against disobedience as shown in 1 Kings 13?
options: Hebrews 10:26-31
Matthew 5:9
Acts 2:38
Revelation 22:21
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 10:26-31
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:26-31 discusses judgment for willful sin, paralleling the judgment against disobedience in 1 Kings 13:21-24.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine attribute is demonstrated when the man of God's sign causes the altar to be rent and ashes to be poured out?
options: God's omnipotence in executing judgment
God's mercy toward sinners
God's patience in waiting for repentance
God's grace in forgiving sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence in executing judgment
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 13:3 and 1 Kings 13:5, God demonstrates His omnipotence by causing the altar to be rent and ashes to be poured out as a sign, showing His power to execute judgment directly.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 13:2, what prophetic event concerning the house of David is foretold by the man of God at Bethel?
options: A child named Josiah will be born who will offer priests on the altar
A child named Solomon will rebuild the temple
A child named David will reign forever
A child named Hezekiah will destroy the high places
questions.correctAnswer: A child named Josiah will be born who will offer priests on the altar
questions.explanation: Verse 2 clearly states that a child shall be born to the house of David named Josiah, who will offer priests on the altar and burn men's bones upon it, indicating a future judgment and reform.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the man of God's punishment and death for disobedience in this chapter?
options: The doctrine of divine judgment for disobedience
The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of eternal security
The doctrine of universal grace
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine judgment for disobedience
questions.explanation: The man of God disobeyed God's command and faced immediate death (1 Kings 13:21-24), illustrating the doctrine that divine judgment is certain for willful disobedience to God's word.

questions.question: In the narrative, what role does the old prophet of Bethel play in the theological unfolding of the story?
options: He acts as a false prophet who deceives the man of God
He is a faithful prophet who restores the man of God
He serves as a symbol of God's mercy
He represents the king's loyal advisor
questions.correctAnswer: He acts as a false prophet who deceives the man of God
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 13:18-19, the old prophet lies to the man of God claiming an angel told him to bring him back, leading to the man of God's disobedience and death, showing the danger of false prophecy.

questions.question: What does the drying up of Jeroboam’s hand when he stretched it out to seize the man of God reveal about God’s sovereignty?
options: God sovereignly controls human actions to fulfill His purposes
God limits human authority over prophets
God uses miracles only for mercy
God avoids confrontation with kings
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls human actions to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 13:4, Jeroboam’s hand is dried up when he tries to seize the man of God, showing that God sovereignly intervenes in human affairs to accomplish His will.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 13:9 teach the doctrine of obedience to God's specific commands?
options: By commanding the man of God not to eat bread or drink water in the land
By allowing the man of God to choose his path freely
By emphasizing the importance of prayer before action
By showing that God's commands can be disregarded
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding the man of God not to eat bread or drink water in the land
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states God's command to the man of God to abstain from eating and drinking in that place and not to return by the same way, emphasizing strict obedience to God's instructions.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 1 Kings 13:21-22 and 1 Kings 13:24 convey about sin and its consequences?
options: Sin leads to temporal judgment and the loss of a proper burial
Sin is always forgiven immediately upon repentance
Sin has no consequences if one is a prophet
Sin results only in spiritual, not physical, consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to temporal judgment and the loss of a proper burial
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 show judgment because of disobedience, and verse 24 describes the man of God’s death and his body being left unburied on the road, indicating temporal consequences of sin.

questions.question: What does the man of God's refusal to accept Jeroboam's invitation in 1 Kings 13:8-10 reveal about prophetic integrity?
options: Prophetic integrity requires strict adherence to God's commands
Prophets can be bribed to soften their message
Prophetic messages are flexible depending on circumstances
Prophets should accept royal hospitality to gain favor
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic integrity requires strict adherence to God's commands
questions.explanation: The man of God refuses Jeroboam's offer because he was commanded by God not to eat or drink there or return the same way, showing that prophetic integrity depends on obedience to divine instructions (1 Kings 13:8-10).

questions.question: How does this chapter contribute to the biblical theology of the consequences of false prophecy, as seen in 1 Kings 13:18 and 1 Kings 13:26?
options: It shows that false prophecy brings about judgment on both the deceiver and the deceived
It suggests that false prophecy has no real consequences
It emphasizes that false prophets are always forgiven
It implies that false prophecy is a minor issue
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that false prophecy brings about judgment on both the deceiver and the deceived
questions.explanation: Verse 18 reveals the old prophet lied, and verse 26 shows God's judgment on the man of God for disobedience due to that lie, illustrating serious consequences of false prophecy.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by Jeroboam's continued sin and the making of priests from the lowest of the people according to 1 Kings 13:33-34?
options: The doctrine of corporate sin affecting a dynasty
The doctrine of individual salvation
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of sacramentalism
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of corporate sin affecting a dynasty
questions.explanation: Jeroboam’s unrepentant sin and consecration of unqualified priests led to judgment on his house (verse 34), showing how sin can corporately affect a dynasty and its legacy.

questions.question: What is the redemptive significance of the prophecy concerning Josiah in 1 Kings 13:2 when viewed in the grand narrative of Scripture?
options: It foreshadows Christ's ultimate judgment on false worship
It predicts the building of the Second Temple
It refers to the coming of Elijah
It describes the exile of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ's ultimate judgment on false worship
questions.explanation: Josiah's judgment on the idolatrous priests and altars (verse 2) typologically points to Christ's ultimate judgment on false worship and the restoration of true worship in redemptive history.

questions.question: What is the apologetics response to the sceptical claim that God’s commands in 1 Kings 13 are contradictory and unjust, based on the man of God’s experience and death?
options: God’s commands are just and must be obeyed even if they result in severe discipline
God’s commands are arbitrary and therefore not to be trusted
The man of God’s death shows God’s wrath is unpredictable
The story is a myth and not historical
questions.correctAnswer: God’s commands are just and must be obeyed even if they result in severe discipline
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 13:21-24 teaches that disobedience to God's explicit commands results in just discipline, demonstrating God's holiness and justice, which is consistent with His righteous character (Exodus 34:6-7).

questions.question: How does the narrative arc of 1 Kings 13 illustrate the tension between God's sovereign word and human free will?
options: God’s sovereign word is authoritative but humans must choose obedience or face consequences
God forces humans to obey without choice
Human free will overrides God’s commands
God’s word is suggestive rather than mandatory
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign word is authoritative but humans must choose obedience or face consequences
questions.explanation: The man of God had a clear command but chose to obey the false prophet instead, leading to judgment (1 Kings 13:9, 18-24), showing that God's word is sovereign but humans are responsible for their choices.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by combining 1 Kings 13:29-31 concerning burial and 1 Kings 13:2 about judgment on the altar?
options: Proper burial symbolizes respect for God's judgment and prophecy fulfillment
Burial practices are irrelevant to divine judgment
The altar’s judgment negates the need for burial
Burial ensures forgiveness of sins
questions.correctAnswer: Proper burial symbolizes respect for God's judgment and prophecy fulfillment
questions.explanation: The old prophet’s request to be buried beside the man of God (verses 29-31) honors the fulfillment of the prophecy made at the altar in verse 2, affirming respect for God's word and judgment.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in 1 Kings 13:6 when the man of God intercedes for Jeroboam’s hand to be restored?
options: God's mercy and responsiveness to prayer
God's wrathful judgment without reprieve
God's indifference to human suffering
God's unconditional favor regardless of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and responsiveness to prayer
questions.explanation: In verse 6, after the man of God prays, Jeroboam’s hand is restored, indicating God’s attribute of mercy and His responsiveness to intercessory prayer.
